outcome: Phase 3 step 4 of the latency plan: a monitoring edit that changes only exclusions no longer reads the registries again and keeps the decisions of every candidate it does not name. On the household installation the server save total fell from a median 1.96 s to 1.33 s, the client save response from 2.20 s to 1.41 s and the settled panel from 2.38 s to 1.52 s; one of six edits still caught a generation-2 collection of 0.87 s. A first attempt that cached the scan without excluding it from the save checkpoint made checkpoint creation 0.3 s slower; the shipped change excludes the cache and the trace bookkeeping from the checkpoint's deep copy.
plan: Homeostatic save and refresh latency investigation plan, phase 3 step 4 (fix by measured share with a live before and after)

status.code_changes: custom_components/homeostatic/runtime.py: _discover(rescan=...) reuses the last registry scan when the settings the scan reads (functions, policy selections, enabled flags) are unchanged and no registry or state-metadata event marked the inventory dirty; the save path passes rescan=self._inventory_dirty; the reconcile timer and every event-driven refresh still scan; the scan cache and the trace bookkeeping are excluded from the save checkpoint's deep copy. custom_components/homeostatic/enrollment.py: evaluate() keeps a candidate's earlier decision when the rule sets differ only in exclusions, the candidate's exclusion did not change and its source is unchanged (changed_exclusions). tests/test_discovery_reuse.py: an exclusion edit reads no registry and re-decides only the named ids; selection changes, registry changes and the reconcile tick still scan.
